title: nightlab-skim-spark-notes-keira-2026-10
content:
NightLab quick skim + late-night sparks (raw)

Context: ran through 3 papers + two blog posts during the flight. Trying to capture the mental thread for follow-ups at the lab tomorrow. Mostly hypotheses, shaky sketches, and quick micro-bench ideas — not polished.

Paper skim 1: "Efficient KV Sharding for Long-Context LMs" (arXiv)
- core idea: split KV cache across shards keyed by token-range / recentness; local hits served from small LRU slices, remote fetch fallback with async prefetch
- interesting: graded staleness—older KV segments served at lower precision or via compressed representations
- takeaway for Redwood: could integrate graded-precision read path when routing to dedicated vs hosted variants (cheap tier gets compressed-history reads)
- open question: eviction policy interacts badly with sampling-based decoding (beam/beam-like). need to simulate with our beam workloads.
- micro experiment: adapt our 8k->32k ctx bench to 1) shard KV by chunk, 2) store chunk metadata (min token idx, average entropy), measure hit rate + avg latency at varying chunk sizes (128,512,2048).

Paper skim 2: "Prefix Distillation with Adaptive Memory" (conference short)
- compress long context into a learned prefix (small) + pointer map; model uses prefix + sparse pointers to reconstruct salient tokens
- nice for bursty access patterns where only a few earlier segments matter
- potential integration: offline prefix distill step in Redwood Optimize as a suggestion for customers with stable prompt families
- cheap UX idea: console shows "prefix retention estimate" and suggested retention window -> actionable knob for ops teams

Paper skim 3: "Quantized Retrieval-Augmented Generation Tradeoffs"
- experiments show 4-bit quantization on retriever vectors OK for recall, but downstream reranking suffers if quant noise aligns with query distribution
- practical rule: keep 8-bit for last-mile reranker; quantize archive vectors aggressively
- for Redwood Dedicated pricing: recommend a two-tier storage: cold highly-quantized archive + hot 8-bit reranker store. Could be part of Optimize recommendations.

Blog notes: engineering post about "asynchronous KV streaming for low-latency decode"
- implement small async fetch pipeline: decode consumes local KV, triggers background fetch for remote shards, integrates when ready. If integrated before decode reaches that span, latency hit minimal
- caveat: correctness for deterministic sampling requires blocking on certain tokens; need to characterize which tokens are safety-critical.

Sketch: unified experiment plan (night-to-morning)
- baseline: current production 8k context, batch size 1, greedy / sampling recipes we use in Hosted API tests
- variant A: shard-KV with on-demand remote fetch (sync), chunk sizes [256,512,1024]
- variant B: shard-KV with async prefetch + merge, same chunk sizes; measure tail latency (95/99), token-per-second throughput, and extra network ops per request
- variant C: prefix-distill pipeline (offline), run rerun synthetic prompts (customer-replay traces), measure perplexity and human-eval drop (small set)
- metrics to capture: 95/99 latency, additional bytes transmitted, CPU on host, GPU stall time, qualitative failure modes (mismatch/inconsistent generations)

Quick hack notes (commands / diffs to try)
- start from branch: prototypes/context-cache-experiments (see PR #42)
- add a metric: kv-remote-fetch-latency-ms and kv-prefetch-hit boolean to tracing headers
- small config toggle: PREFETCH_WINDOW_TOKENS=512 (env) to test prefetch threshold
- local test harness: replay-tool --trace sample_customer_replays/marketing-bot-2026-08.json --seed 42 --mode decode

Open doubts (need concrete answers)
- how often do our hosted customers use deterministic decoding in ways that prevent async integration? (ask Solutions Engs)
- what is the network topology for Dedicated customers btw inference shards? do we run within same AZ or across AZs? affects fetch latency assumptions
- long tail: eviction spikes during synthetic long convo tests — is it config (KV LRU) or bug in merge logic? replicate with unit tests that randomize access patterns.

Follow-ups / Action items
- morning: pair with Devin to run variant A/B at 9am — 2 hour slot on staging nodes (tag: run-id nightlab-2026-10-23-1)
- ping Mira to check whether Solutions Eng has deterministic-decoding customers; add to meeting notes
- draft a short console mockup showing "prefix retention estimate" and store-tier recommendation for Optimize (10–15m mock)
- write a tiny eval harness that marks a request as "needs-determinism" if any callsite set seed != -1 or using beam>1 — instrumented in replay harness

Random sidebar thoughts (brain-dump)
- could we expose an "approximate history" endpoint that returns compressed context summary instead of raw tokens? privacy + bandwidth friendly for some apps
- billing question: if we serve compressed history (approx prefix) at lower token-cost, do we need different metering? maybe count "history-qual units"? product needs a short spec.
- team idea: run a lightning study with 5 customers (volunteer) to test prefix-distill suggestion in Optimize beta. incentives: credits + engineering consult.

References & quick links I kept open
- arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14300 (sharding kv)
- our PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prototypes/context-cache-experiments/pull/42
- slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02EXAMPLE/p1680000000000

Notes-to-self
- keep this doc short-lived; move polished experiment plan to product/optimize/notes after morning pairing
- capture run-id/timestamps in the PR so we can match traces to experiments

-- Keira
